change.title: pr-6
change.description: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain
change.author: Arpit Jalan

findings.title: website_name leaks the website host of restricted TL0 users to anonymous viewers
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so `include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. That is a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor (lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58). `website_name` is not in that list, and `include_website_name` (line 153) only checks `website.present?`. The API therefore still returns the website host and path for those users. The old client-side `websiteName` came from `model.website`, which was hidden, so nothing showed. Now the profile header renders the hidden website, as a link with no href. This defeats the anti-spam restriction. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` call. Alternatively, make `include_website_name` return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`, then check `website.present?`. Add a spec for it.

findings.title: website_name goes stale after the user edits their website in preferences
findings.body: The template now reads `model.website_name`, which comes from the server. The old controller property was computed from `model.website`, so it updated as soon as the value changed. `User.save` sends `website` (line 171). Its success handler only copies `bio_excerpt` back from the response (line 210). The PUT response is a `UserSerializer` payload (app/controllers/users_controller.rb:100) and already includes `website_name`. The same user model object is shown on the profile page afterwards. After saving a new website and going back to the profile, the header shows the old name, or nothing if there was none, until a full reload. There is no error or other visible sign. Set `website_name` from `data.user.website_name` in the `.then` handler. When the website is cleared the attribute is omitted, so this also clears the stale value.

findings.title: website_name re-parses the URI up to three times and has avoidable edge cases
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed on lines 138, 143, 146 and 149, and only the first is rescued. Parse once into a local variable instead. A URI with a trailing-slash root (`http://example.com/`) gives `example.com/` on the same domain. The host is not downcased before it is compared with `Discourse.current_hostname`, so `http://Example.com/x` will not match. Line 149 uses `"." << website_host`, which mutates a string literal and would raise under frozen string literals. Use `".#{website_host}"`.

findings.title: Missing coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch, restricted users and an unparsable website
findings.body: The three examples cover only the unrelated-domain, same-domain and parent-domain branches. They do not cover the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch (serializer lines 144-146). They do not cover a TL0 user viewed anonymously, where `website_name` must be absent (see the security finding). They do not cover a website that does not parse, or one with no scheme, where `website_name` is nil.

contracts.action: Profile header shows website name from server-provided website_name instead of controller-computed websiteName
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed UserController.websiteName computed property, derived from model.website (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/user.js.es6, removed lines 17-21)
contracts.before_after: Before: computed live from model.website, hidden whenever website was hidden or changed. After: read from model.website_name, which is set only when the user JSON loads (UserSerializer line 43). It is not refreshed in User.save (models/user.js.es6:210) and is not subject to untrusted_attributes.
contracts.visible_effect: Header shows the host, or host+path on the same domain. It can be stale after a preferences edit, and it appears for restricted TL0 users even though website is hidden.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent: wrong or stale text with no error.

summary: The change is functionally correct for the happy path, but it has two silent defects. `website_name` is not covered by the TL0/anonymous restriction that hides `website`, so it leaks the hidden website host. The client also never refreshes `website_name` after a profile save, so the header goes stale. I also noted cleanup in the host logic and a few missing spec cases.
